title: Corporate Tax Manager
description: About Unity Advisory Unity Advisory is a modern advisory business built for today's CFO, with connected solutions across finance, deals and tax. Focussed on client outcomes, seasoned experts lead every engagement, in an operating model powered by AI and free from audit conflict. The Role We’re looking for a Manager based in either our London or Manchester office to join Unity Advisory’s growing corporate tax team. You’ll manage a portfolio of advisory and compliance engagements, helping CFOs and finance teams navigate tax obligations, business growth and change. Technology and AI are built into how we work. You’ll use digital tools to improve analysis, streamline delivery and produce clear, practical advice, applying your technical judgement throughout. Working with senior colleagues, you’ll build client relationships, develop junior team members and help shape how we deliver our services. Responsibilities Manage day-to-day delivery across a portfolio of corporate tax clients, acting as their main point of contact. Deliver advice on corporate structuring, reorganisations and tax planning, with senior support on complex matters. Use AI, automation and data analysis to improve delivery, checking outputs for accuracy and technical quality. Prepare and review corporation tax computations, returns and technical reports, managing deadlines and identifying risks. Manage routine HMRC correspondence and enquiries, escalating complex issues where needed. Support transaction-related projects alongside M&A Tax and Deals colleagues. Coach junior colleagues, review their work and manage engagement budgets and resources. Identify opportunities to support clients further and contribute to proposals and pitches. Qualifications and experience Strong UK corporate tax knowledge, with experience delivering advisory and compliance work. Confidence using data and digital tools, with a practical interest in applying AI and automation to improve how you work. CTA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent qualification. Relevant corporate tax experience gained in an in-house team or tax advisory firm, including managing complex assignments and reviewing junior colleagues’ work. Clear communication skills and the ability to explain technical issues in commercial terms. Good organisation, sound judgement and the initiative to take ownership while knowing when to seek support. title: Product Marketing Manager
description: An Introduction to Primer Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform. Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on. Watch our showcase > Read up on our $100m Series C Learn more about our culture > Which team will you be joining? You're joining our Product Marketing team that owns product positioning, launch strategy, and market adoption for Primer's core product lines. We operate as strategic partners embedded in each major domain, working alongside Product and Sales leadership to define how our products win in market. Our PMMs own end-to-end strategy and execution for a significant product area, which means your work gets seen, shaped, and acted on by senior leadership from day one. You'll report to our Product Marketing Lead and work directly with product leads, marketing leads and senior stakeholders across the business. What will you be doing? Core Focus: This is an individual contributor (IC) role providing end-to-end product marketing support for our newly built Partners team. This role needs attention to detail, creativity, and boldness to build out the product's market presence. Own the Partner marketing engine: Driving go-to-market launches from strategy to execution, collaborating closely with the broader marketing team. Work with Partner PMs and Commercial Teams to define target audiences and craft clear, compelling messaging and positioning that differentiates Primer's Partner capabilities in the market. Translate technical products into messaging that lands with both partners and the merchants who benefit from them. Synthesise partner and merchant feedback, sales signals, and market research into a coherent strategic perspective that shapes both messaging and GTM approach. Monitor and report on the effectiveness of product marketing initiatives, using data to optimise strategies and achieve business goals. What we're looking for: Must-haves: 4+ years of B2B SaaS marketing or product marketing experience, , with a track record of launching and growing successful B2B products. Comfort turning technical product detail into messaging a non-technical buyer or partner wants to read. Ability to conduct targeted competitive and buyer research and turn it into specific recommendations. Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Experiment-minded, taking full ownership of outcomes and driving work with minimal oversight. Nice-to-haves: Background in payments, fintech, or infrastructure products (or willingness to build that domain knowledge quickly) Creative judgment - you can brief teams and agencies authoritatively and push for sharper, more unexpected ideas Experience marketing in a two-sided marketplace, balancing distinct value propositions for supply-side and demand-side audiences Why you may not like it here: We move fast. A Tier 1 launch plan that takes months to build is too slow. You'll be making calls on strategy, sequencing, and messaging trade-offs on tighter timelines. All roles at Primer involve hands-on execution to drive maximum impact. If you want to set direction and hand off delivery to someone else, this might not be the fit. You'll work alongside sharp, opinionated stakeholders in sales and product who will pressure-test your ideas. The best PMMs here treat that pushback as a chance to sharpen their thinking with data, not as a hurdle to clear before moving on. ✅ A typical interview process An initial intro call with a Talent Partner An interview with the Hiring Manager Challenge Stage - Contextualised to the role A final, values-alignment interview What's the culture like at Primer? We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants. We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities. The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone. At Primer, we're dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. title: FP&A Manager
description: LemFi (Series B) is building the go-to financial app for the Global South. Moving to a new country shouldn’t mean starting from zero. That's why our team of 400+ spanning 20+ countries is building a financial ecosystem that helps immigrants stay connected to home, build stability, and create wealth regardless of where they are from or where they live. What began as fast, affordable remittances is now evolving into a complete platform for multi-currency accounts, payments, credit, and long-term financial growth. With millions of users across the globe, we process over $1B in monthly transactions to 30+ countries, proving that borders shouldn't limit financial opportunity. About the role LemFi is building the financial home for the world's immigrants - multi-currency accounts, remittances, savings, credit and eSIMs across 21 countries and growing. Strategic Finance sits at the centre of that growth: we hold the forecast, challenge the numbers and make sure leadership and investors see a clear, honest picture of the business. This is the first hire into the FP&A function, reporting directly to the Head of Strategic Finance and FP&A. You will own the full engine: the integrated model, the monthly forecast and BvA cycle, the management pack, and investor and lender reporting. Your numbers go in front of the Board, our investors and our lenders. You will work hand-in-hand with department heads across Growth, Product, Operations and Risk, and have direct exposure to the executive team on commercial and strategic decisions. What you'll build and own Run the monthly forecast and integrated three-statement model - cash runway, revenue, headcount and provider costs - keeping every model reconciled to actuals and documented to a standard anyone can follow. Own the BvA cycle end to end: gather commentary, challenge variances, and hold budget owners accountable for their numbers every single month. Produce the monthly management pack and KPI reporting for the executive team and Board, and prepare investor and lender reporting including covenant and facility tracking. Partner with budget owners across Growth, Product, Operations and Risk on their plans, forecasts and spend - be the finance voice that pushes back with data, not just a service desk. Build robust business cases for new products, corridors, markets and partnerships, including scenario and sensitivity analysis for leadership and the Board. Support fundraising, M&A modelling and diligence as needed - your models will be in the data room. Pull, structure and automate recurring data from NetSuite, the data warehouse and operational systems, using AI where it saves you time and improves accuracy. Your experience 3-5 years in FP&A, strategic finance, transaction services or a modelling-heavy consultancy role (Big 4, strategy or deals). Excellent three-statement modelling skills: driver-based forecasting, scenario and sensitivity analysis, built cleanly and to best-practice standards. Solid accounting foundations: you can link P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, and reconcile a forecast to the ledger without hand-holding. Strong data skills and confidence with large datasets; comfortable pulling and structuring data independently. Clear, direct communicator: you can explain the numbers to non-finance stakeholders and push back where the numbers do not support a decision. High ownership and attention to detail - you do not wait to be asked and you do not let things fall through the cracks in a fast-moving environment. Nice to have Capital markets exposure: equity fundraising, debt facilities, investor reporting or M&A diligence. Experience in payments, remittance, lending or another regulated financial services business. NetSuite, BI tools, SQL or automation experience (Python or similar); professional qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or CFA). Why Join LemFi? Love shouldn’t be expensive, yet those working hardest for their families often face predatory fees and banking exclusion. We're changing this. At LemFi, you won’t be just a cog in a machine. Whether designing products, scaling operations, or telling our story, you’ll tackle complex challenges with real, immediate impact. Your work goes beyond metrics - it puts money back in families’ pockets and offers access to the previously excluded. Join us to make a meaningful difference, where high performance is a lifeline for millions. You can connect with us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play . Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

About the role As UK Entity Controller, reporting to the Head of Financial Control and Reporting, you will own the numbers for our largest and most regulated group of entities: an FCA-authorised e-money institution, a payment institution and our growing consumer credit business. You will lead a small team, run a close the business can rely on every month, and build credit accounting that scales as lending grows. This is a role for a senior controller who genuinely likes ownership. LemFi moves fast, our product surface is expanding and the regulatory bar is high. You will help shape a finance function that is lean, well-controlled and built to last - and you will leave clear fingerprints on how we do things. What you'll build and own Own the UK close - deliver an accurate monthly, quarterly and year-end close for every UK entity on the Group timetable, with every material balance substantiated and independently reviewed. Prepare and file FRS 102 statutory accounts on time, act as the auditors' first point of contact for the UK, and track every audit finding and management letter point through to resolution with clear owners and dates. Build and own credit accounting for our consumer credit business: loan book, IFRS 9 expected credit loss, interest and fee income, write-offs and funding facilities - documented, auditable and scalable. Get safeguarding right - sign off the safeguarding requirement calculation for each UK regulated entity and ensure safeguarded funds and customer balances are correctly reflected, reconciled and agreed with Data, Treasury and Reconciliation at month-end. Account accurately for high volumes of multi-currency transactions including FX revaluation and processor and bank balances, and partner with Group Reporting to agree intercompany positions. Partner with FP&A on entity-level forecasts, evaluate capital adequacy and flag rectification needs ahead of regulatory reporting deadlines; give Tax and Regulatory Finance teams reliable data for FCA returns. Raise the control bar - document processes and internal controls, close gaps, embed maker/checker review and segregation of duties, give every critical task a trained backup, and work with Finance Systems and Data to automate close tasks and build reporting that scales. title: Senior Creative Project Manager - Brand
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role The Creative Production studio team sits squarely within our Brand function working alongside our Brand Foundations team. You will report directly to the Director of Brand Strategy & Experience and join a tight-knit, highly experienced group of project management leads and producers. In this role, you will lead our internal Creative Production studio team, the execution engine delivering all branded assets across Pleo, including campaign and performance assets, global adaptation and localization, event branding, content marketing, web, socials and lifecycle design. You will balance hands-on delivery with direct people management for a team of three in-house designers and copywriter, ensuring our creative output remains fast, scalable, and sharp across all touchpoints. Who you’ll be working with and reporting to Our Brand department is 13 people across two teams: Brand Foundations and Creative Production. You'll lead the four-person Creative Production studio, a senior copywriter, two senior designers and a motion designer, spread across our European offices. Day to day, you'll work alongside a peer project lead on Brand Foundations, a brand strategist, our producers, and internal partners in Events, Lifecycle, Performance Marketing, HR/People Ops and Legal, plus our media agency. Most of the studio's clients are internal teams across Pleo. What you’ll be doing As a Senior Creative Project Manager, you will: Creative Production & Operations Studio Ownership: Lead end-to-end execution across all creative production studio work streams, ensuring projects hit quality benchmarks, deadlines, and brand standards. This is also not just intake of brand requests but also spotting opportunities proactively for brand involvement and governance across the business. Project Management: Own intake of BAU requests, filtering and assigning work while acting as the bridge between requestors and the studio team. Define scope upfront and ensure the team has what it needs to execute. Contribute to project plans for integrated campaigns and large events and manage Creative studio kick-offs, status reporting, and timeline and milestone tracking. Core Output Focus: Oversee production for high-performing marketing assets, market localization and adaptations, event branding, and content marketing. Process & Integration: Partner closely with peer project leads, producers, and the Brand Foundations team to streamline intake briefs, cross-team handoffs, and resource sharing. Global Asset Delivery: Manage asset adaptation frameworks to keep our brand consistent across different regions and channels. Capacity Planning: Own and manage resourcing across internal teams and freelance support, balancing capacity against demand and prioritizing against business needs when demands compete. External agency partnerships: Serve as the lead creative point of contact for asset production with our media agency. Manage sprint-style monthly asset delivery in response to agency and internal performance team briefs, keeping output aligned with the media plan. Review final creative placements across Meta and LinkedIn to ensure assets display correctly on paid channels. People Management & Leadership Direct Management: Line manage, mentor, and foster career growth for a cross-functional team of three in-house designers and one copywriter overseeing their daily priorities and bandwidth. Stakeholder Alignment & Strategy Cross-Functional Partner: Serve as the strategic operational bridge connecting the studio with Marketing, Events, HR/People Ops, and Legal. Leadership Alignment: Work closely with the Director of Brand Strategy & Experience and Associate Director of Brand Management to align studio output with broader brand goals and business priorities. We launched our new brand in September, so this is a moment to build. The studio has the basics in place, but intake, briefing, project tracking and resourcing are still early. You'll set the ways of working that the studio runs on, and we'd love you to bring AI into how we plan, brief and produce. What you bring You'll thrive in this role if you have: In-House Brand Experience: Minimum 5-7 years of work experience. Solid background working in-house in a fast-paced brand function (tech, scale-up, or high-growth environment). People Leadership: Direct experience line-managing creative talent (designers/artworkers) based remotely in different offices in Europe with an empathetic, growth-oriented approach. Production Scope: Broad familiarity managing workflows across digital performance, multi-market localization, physical/virtual events, AI creative production, and employer branding. Culture Driver: Thrives in a peer environment working alongside other motivated and constructive senior PMs, producers, creatives, and strategists. Operational Skills: Mastery of modern project management tooling and AI-powered workflows (e.g. Asana, Notion, Jira, Slack). Project Management Experience: Strong hands-on project management experience in a fast-paced, delivery-focused environment, running multiple projects concurrently. Comfortable not just initiating projects, but staying a consistent presence throughout: managing delivery, and reassessing priorities and capacity as needs shift. Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You love day-to-day production and get a kick out of turning an event brief into finished collateral within a week. You want to build how a studio works, from intake to resourcing, as much as you want to ship the work. You enjoy leading creatives, giving them clear briefs and keeping the work grounded in what the business needs. This role is not a good fit for you if: You mainly want to work on big brand campaigns. We run around two a year, and they're produced with an external agency. The studio adapts those assets, but most of the work is events, performance creative and BAU requests. You prefer a predictable, planned workload. Last-minute requests are part of life on Brand. You haven't line-managed people yet. Direct people management of the studio team is a core part of this role. How you’ll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll: Deliver the studio's day-to-day work to our speed and quality standards, in line with the new brand guidelines. Set best practice for how the studio takes in, briefs, tracks and resources work. Improve how we estimate and plan capacity, using AI where it makes sense. The location Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations. Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. Hiring manager interview: A conversation with the Director about the projects you've delivered, the teams you've led and the kind of production work you enjoy most. Case study: You'll walk us through how you'd approach a creative production task. You'll present to the Director and a peer project lead, and possibly a member of the studio team. Final stage: Team-fit chat with one or two people from the studio Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired this role, we received an incredibly high volume of applications but only so many could be taken forward. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background! Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes per

description: <div class="content-intro"><h2>About us</h2> <div><strong>Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence<br></strong><br>PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.</div></div><h2>The Role</h2> <p>PhysicsX is building a platform that enables Data Scientists and Simulation Engineers to build, train, and deploy Deep Physics Models. The platform handles massive volumes of complex simulation data and enables high fidelity multi physics simulation through AI inference.</p> <p>We are looking for a Senior (potentially Staff level, depending on the candidate) Software Engineer to join the AI Workbench platform team. This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need to be a practising ML engineer, but you do need to be fluent in the language of ML and data platforms, ideally through prior hands on experience with ML platforms or data science work.</p> <p>The team sits in a highly infrastructure heavy domain without being an infrastructure team itself. Strong working knowledge of the Salesforce data model, including standard objects (e.g., Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case, User) and custom objects, relationships (lookup and master-detail), record types, and field types. Strong SQL Server and T-SQL skills, including stored procedures, joins across large data sets, performance tuning, and data quality checks. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start: One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK Profitable since 2017 Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot ) So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. Join us if you want to Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1 Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting Lendable is revolutionising the credit card industry by making financial tools accessible, intuitive, and empowering. Zable is a Mobile-App first credit card that empowers customers to build their credit score while meeting their spending and borrowing needs sustainably. We’re looking for an analytical, commercially-minded Senior Strategy Analyst to help us grow and scale the product exponentially . This is a dynamic role where you’ll tackle high impact business problems across a number of disciplines including pricing, financial forecasting, growth, credit risk, new product development and product analytics. You’ll help us solve our most complex multi-dimensional challenges, working cross-functionally to deliver insight-driven strategies that optimise performance, drive responsible growth, and put the customer at the heart of decision-making. You’ll operate in a fast-paced environment where ideas matter more than hierarchy, and execution beats bureaucracy. Your work will directly influence who we serve, how we grow, and how we deliver sustainable value. Key Responsibilities Drive promotions & pricing strategy: Develop and optimise promotional and pricing strategies through data-driven analysis and experimentation, balancing customer engagement, growth, price elasticity and profitability while continuously refining approaches based on product performance and scenario modelling. Build deep insight into marketing campaign and conversion funnel performance, identifying opportunities to improve cost and conversion efficiency. Stay abreast of industry trends and competitor activity to ensure our products remain fit for purpose. Financial forecasting & portfolio analytics: Collaborate closely with the Credit Risk Analytics, Growth and Data Science teams to understand how our products and portfolio are performing at a granular sub-segment level. Define key KPIs and develop detailed monitoring to track performance against these goals, and deliver actionable recommendations to improve outcomes. Use strategic analysis to shape and influence broader business strategy. Evaluate expansion opportunities: Navigate through ambiguity to assess the feasibility of new product, channel and segment expansion opportunities. Create robust commercial assessment frameworks, build tooling where necessary (e.g. RoI or NPV models) and extract data to support these assessments and deliver clear, insight-driven recommendations. Influence & execution: Collaborate with stakeholders across Credit Risk, Data Science, Product and Growth to bring your strategies to life. Present insights and recommendations to senior leadership - clear, concise, and backed by data. Approach every conversation with an open mind, valuing the strength of ideas over ego or hierarchy. Ensure your implemented strategies are working as intended once deployed in production, validating outcomes and iterating as needed. Fast-track your career growth: Opportunity to mentor and coach more junior graduate analysts, fostering their technical growth and strategic thinking. Well defined career progression pathways to Manager/Senior Manager for high performers. Your experience Essential: 3+ years of experience in an analytics role in any discipline (e.g. Growth, Credit Risk, Product Analytics, Marketing, etc.) Proficiency in coding - ideally SQL and Python Desirable: Experience in an FCA-regulated financial services firm Life at Lendable Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner. Check out our blog ! Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Strategic delivery lead
description: Hybrid role requiring three days a week in our London or Edinburgh office About us Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well. We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology powers some of the UK’s most ambitious and forward-thinking banks, fintechs, financial advisers and wealth firms, giving them the software and services they need to launch and grow investment propositions at pace. We’ve grown rapidly to reach the scale of some of the UK’s largest investment platforms. Today, more than one million people – around 5% of UK investors – rely on Seccl to power their investment experience. And we’re now expanding into Europe. We’re proud to be part of Octopus, a group with a track record of using technology to transform established industries. Our sister company, Octopus Energy, has grown from a UK start-up into a global energy and technology business, while its now-demerged Kraken platform supports tens of millions of accounts around the world. We share that ambition to use better technology to transform an industry – replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for the future. Like Octopus, we’re a B Corp-certified company, with a firm belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand. If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and Europe, you’ll be in good company. Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments. The role You’ll join our strategic delivery team, reporting to our head of strategic delivery, and lead some of Seccl’s biggest and most complex programmes. These could include managing our entry to new markets, overseeing the onboarding of major new customers, tackling significant re-platforming projects or launching new operating models. You’ll take responsibility for a programme end to end – turning a strategic or commercial objective into a workable plan, bringing together the right people from across Seccl and driving the decisions needed to get it delivered. You’ll work across the business – collaborating with our product, engineering, operations, commercial, risk and finance teams, as well as directly with senior stakeholders at our customer firms. These programmes will be of significant commercial value and come with real complexity, so you’ll need to build strong relationships, make difficult calls and know when something genuinely needs escalating. What you’ll be accountable for... You will: Own complex strategic programmes end to end, from business case and mobilisation through to launch, migration and handover Build the business case, delivery plan, team and governance needed to get a programme moving Lead cross-functional delivery across Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Risk, Finance and other teams Drive decisions and resolve blockers, while managing risks, dependencies, scope, cost and timelines Lead commercial discussions with customer firms where needed, working closely with Commercial and Legal Run readiness and go/no-go decisions, then closing programmes against their original business case This role’s for you if... You have a background in financial services, fintech or another regulated industry and understand the complexity that comes with delivering significant change You have experience leading large, complex programmes (such as major re-platforming or new market expansion), and understand the complexities and inter-dependencies involved You’ve independently led complex, high-stakes programmes from start to finish, with accountability for delivery You’re comfortable creating direction and structure where there isn’t an existing playbook, and solving problems as they emerge You build strong relationships and collaborate well across teams, while being confident enough to challenge, hold people to account and make difficult decisions You understand both delivery and the commercial case behind it, including cost, value and trade-offs You’re strong at cross-functional dependency and risk management and know when to make the call yourself This role isn’t for you if... You want a ready-made playbook. You’ll often need to create the structure and delivery approach yourself You prefer a narrow programme management remit. This role works across the business and gets into commercial and strategic decisions You’re quick to escalate difficult decisions. We’ll expect you to use your judgement and operate with a high level of autonomy You’d rather avoid customer-facing commercial conversations. Some programmes will involve working directly with senior customer stakeholders What’s in it for you We offer a generous mix of benefits designed around the things that matter to our people: 💰 A salary of £85,000-£115,000, reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance 🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays , your birthday off and paid dependant leave 💙 Two volunteering days each year 🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year 🌟 Secclbrate , our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget 🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health 👪 Enhanced parental leave 💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up 📖 £750 annual learning budget 🌻 Health and wellbeing support , including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace 🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits , including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy 🎁 Perkbox , with flexible points and a range of discounts and perks 🚲 Access to Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing Our culture We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work. We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You’ll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact. Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team. Interview process Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too. First stage: an initial discussion around your relevant experience and how you work with the hiring manager and another strategic delivery lead Second stage: role-specific assessment with the hiring manager and chief product officer Final stage: a bar raiser interview with our chief technology officer We review applications as they come in and may close the role once we have enough candidates to move forward. We’ll keep you updated throughout. Everyone’s welcome We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability. If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you. title: Senior Product Manager - Direct Hotels
description: Why loveholidays? We’re on a mission to open the world to everyone, giving our customers unlimited choice, unmatched ease and unmissable value for their next getaway. Our trailblaze together culture is what drives our success, powered by our people and the way they work. Using progressive technology, we drive cutting-edge innovation and improve how our customers discover, book and experience their holidays. You’ll have the opportunity to accelerate your growth through meaningful challenges, new experiences and the freedom to shape your own path. You’ll create impact for our future by taking ownership, contributing to shared goals and helping shape what comes next, all as part of our enhanced international community of talented, collaborative and passionate teams. The difference you’ll make You’ll own the products that help loveholidays grow direct relationships with hotels. By making it easier for partners to join us, manage their supply and improve their performance, you’ll help hotels achieve their commercial goals while giving our customers greater choice and value. Our ambition is to build an industry-leading operating system for our suppliers: bringing together onboarding, day-to-day management and the insights partners need to make better commercial decisions. You’ll help turn that ambition into a clear product direction. Your initial focus will be simplifying hotel onboarding and improving how effectively we turn direct hotel supply into bookings. You’ll be part of the Direct Hotels team, reporting to the Head of Product for Supply Platform. Working closely with Engineering, Design, Commercial, Operations and Analytics to build capabilities for hotel partners that support our broader supply strategy. The team sits within Platform, which provides shared technology and tools to help teams across loveholidays deliver the outcomes that drive value for our suppliers and experiences that delight our customers. Your day-to-day: Own the product direction and roadmap. Translate the Direct Hotels ambition into prioritised opportunities, clear outcomes and achievable delivery increments. Make informed trade-offs between supplier needs, commercial value and technical investment. Understand the people using our products. Work directly with hotel partners, contracting teams and loading operations to uncover problems, test ideas and understand what will drive adoption. Improve the journey from onboarding to bookable supply. Simplify how information is collected, checked and maintained, using automation and self-service where they make the experience easier to navigate and more reliable. Build towards supplier self-service. Develop capabilities that progressively give hotels more control over their relationship with us, working towards connected management tools and useful commercial insights. Take products from discovery through to measurable impact. Work closely with Engineering and Design to prototype, test, deliver and iterate. Explore practical applications of AI, define success measures and use evidence from adoption, supplier feedback and commercial performance to guide what comes next. Your skillset: Product ownership and strategic delivery: A track record of taking complex problems from discovery through to delivery and demonstrating meaningful user and business outcomes. You're drawn to figuring out what to build, not just building what's specified.</li> <li>A bias for action. Our clients’ success is our success. </span></li> <li><strong>Drive Innovation - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry. </span></li> <li><strong>Embrace Learning - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Engage our community to broaden our perspective. title: Clinical AI Engineer
description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years. To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund. If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in. The role We’re looking for a doctor who has moved into AI and can code, to join Clinical AI R&D as a Clinical AI Engineer. You’ll sit inside a product pod and own the evidence for its product: define the evaluation before anyone builds, run it to a standard a journal reviewer would accept, keep watching the product once it ships, publish what the evidence shows, and change the product when the evidence says to. The pod’s engineers can change the product but can’t judge whether a discharge summary missed something a consultant would catch. Clinicians can make that call but can’t open a pull request. You do both, and you treat the gap between a model’s output and good clinical practice as the thing you’re here to measure and close. The loop doesn’t end at launch. You stay with the product for its life in market. What you’ll do Design the evaluation. Define evaluations for greenfield products to an academic standard: endpoints, comparators, ground truth, sample size, analysis plan. Set the bar before the result arrives. Build the measurement. Build, optimize and validate the LLM judges and rubrics that score the product at scale. Report their agreement with clinician ground truth, not their convenience, and retire the ones that drift. Run it and write it up. Execute the evaluation, do the statistics, and write it up once in a form that serves the pod, the regulatory file and an academic submission. Run post-market surveillance. Monitor output quality in production and respond to regulatory feedback with data. Our clinical safety team triages complaints and incidents; you’re their counterpart in the pod, working out what their findings mean for the product and what should change. Fix what the evidence finds. Prompt and rubric changes, evaluation harness changes, code changes in the pod’s codebase, shipped through the pod’s normal review and release process. Publish. Contribute to peer-reviewed literature on the translational benefit of the product. Be the clinician in the room. Catch the output that reads well and is wrong. Hold the line on clinical nuance when a shortcut would ship faster. What you'll need A medical degree and clinical practice with independent clinical judgment. This role runs on medical nuance, and this requirement doesn’t flex. Academic depth. Study design, inferential statistics, agreement and reliability measures, sample size, handling of multiple comparisons. Thesis or publication-level work, not a methods module. Experience evaluating medical software or clinical AI, including building or validating LLM-as-judge pipelines. Enough engineering to work in a production codebase. Read it, understand what a change will do, make the change in Python or TypeScript, and get it through review. Prompt engineering and AI-assisted coding are daily tools here, and they’re the floor, not the ceiling. Independence. You can run a project for weeks with light direction, and you say early when it’s stuck. Clear writing. Evaluation reports, surveillance summaries and manuscripts are the primary output of this role. Nice to have Post-market surveillance or vigilance work under a medical device framework (TGA, MHRA, FDA or EU MDR). Appetite to learn counts for more than existing depth. Peer-reviewed publications on clinical AI or LLM evaluation. Machine learning background beyond prompting, such as fine-tuning or classical model evaluation. Specialty depth in an area Heidi is moving into. An academic or clinical-site network able to host a study. How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. Our Benefits Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create. Your health, covered. Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend. Global parental leave . 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility. Fertility support . £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies. Learning & development. £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more. Home office budget of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in. Recharge days after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong. Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes you. Clinical leave . 10 days per year for eligible clinical roles to maintain accreditation and requirements. Flexibility that works. A hybrid environment, with 3 days in the office. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all. title: Principal Product Designer (Ventures)
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Product team defines how millions of people experience Deliveroo, turning complex marketplace challenges into simple, high-impact solutions. Working at the intersection of data, design and engineering, we set direction, prioritise what matters most, and deliver outcomes that move the business forward. We're looking for a Principal Product Designer to join our Ventures team in London. You'll be the senior design voice on an early-stage product, taking it from first concept to a test-market launch and shaping it for global scale. About Ventures Ventures is DoorDash's internal incubator, where we build the next generation of businesses adjacent to our core. We fund small teams with a strong sense of ownership and grow the investment as they hit clear milestones. Early on, teams build a Minimum Lovable Product and prove product-market fit in a single country. Successful initiatives graduate to new resources and new markets, with the chance to become the next billion-euro businesses at DoorDash. Ventures teams are scrappy and ambitious, chase goals that almost feel too ambitious, and thrive on a startup mentality and a high tolerance for ambiguity. We're now placing bigger and more diverse bets than ever, and we need people with equal ambition and drive to build and scale, or sunset, some of our biggest experiments yet. What You'll Be Doing Vision & Influence Define the design vision and strategy across several Ventures products, deciding what to build at product-area level and sequencing work across teams. Become an expert on local market dynamics, ensuring each product is shaped by how people behave in each place. Partner with product-area leadership as a trusted advisor, shaping roadmaps and priorities. Build like a founder: set success metrics, share weekly updates, present at key business reviews and partner with your cross-functional team leads to build the case for further investment. Craft & Leadership Deliver differentiated, step-change improvements to customer journeys in crowded markets. Design scalable foundations across complex journeys, and turn regulatory constraints into simple experiences with legal, finance and operations. Build systems, prototyping frameworks and AI-enhanced workflows, setting the standards that drive adoption. Establish critiques and planning practices, mentor senior designers and emerging leaders, and hire senior designers and first-line managers. What You'll Need to Thrive Product-Area Leadership: Proven experience leading design initiatives across multiple products, including taking more than one from 0-1. Product Judgement: A track record of spotting opportunities that improve long-term outcomes, backed by exceptional craft. Strategic Influence: Credibility with senior leaders and the ability to connect customer research, business goals and feasibility into one strategy. Developing Leaders: A history of coaching designers and managers and recruiting talent that wants to join you. Systems and AI Fluency: Experience building tools and standards that scale across teams. Bias for Action: Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving, startup-style environment. Why Join Us? At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to: 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day. 🌱 See your impact, fast Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment. 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support. 🌎 A culture built for builders High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning. ​​💰 Share in the success you help create Competitive salary and equity options, so you're rewarded for the impact you make. ➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog . We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. title: Client Partner
description: Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets. We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in. Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits. We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors. Why we're hiring We're on track for roughly 700 deals a year and $750m in investment flowing through Odin in 2026. The goal is 7,000 deals a year. Inbound is already around 70 new leads a month and climbing. You won't be cold calling. The demand is here, and your job is to turn it into deals. Our customers are angels, syndicate leads and fund managers backing the most interesting companies in the world. When they're doing a deal, you're the person they call. Every customer you bring in becomes part of your book, and your commission grows with it. You'll be one of the first people in our commercial team, shaping how we sell as we scale from here. What you'll own Converting inbound: A steady flow of inbound lands with you every week. You decide quickly which leads have a real deal behind them and turn them into their first deal on Odin, spending your time where it pays off. Getting every deal to close: You own the deal from first conversation to close, and the customer knows you as their person at Odin. Ops, compliance and legal do the work; you run the deal, know exactly what's closing this week and what's in the way, and make it happen. That's the trust that brings customers back. Your book: Every customer you bring in is yours, and so is their next deal. Over time you build a book of investors backing some of the most interesting companies in the world, and it compounds. Building how we sell: You'll help write the playbook: how we qualify, run first calls, use Attio and Claude, and what we automate. When you find a better way, it becomes how the team works, and you grow as the team does. What we're looking for High-volume inbound sales experience: At least 3 years in a fast, short-cycle SMB or mid-market sales motion, handling lots of inbound and closing against a target, rather than working two enterprise deals a quarter. That could be in tech, but recruitment, ad sales or anywhere else with a fast inbound motion. Extremely organised: You're juggling new leads, live deals and existing customers at once. You prioritise ruthlessly, move fast, and nothing falls through the cracks. Commercial instinct: You read between the lines on a first call, ask the right questions and follow the smoke to find the fire. You can tell a live deal with a closing date from someone browsing. You do what you said you'd do: Customers trust you because you get back to them when you said you would, with the answer they needed. Credible with experienced investors: Comfortable on a call with a seasoned GP or at an event full of them. You'd rather shape it than inherit it: The role is clear, and how we do it is still being built. You want a hand in building it. Big plus: private markets exposure: VC, angel syndicates, fund admin or an SPV platform. Useful, but not required. You'll learn SPV mechanics and fund structuring fast here, and it's rare, valuable expertise to have. How we work There are five things we care about deeply: Reason from the ground up: Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts. Speed begets speed: We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin. Take ownership: Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to. Brutal honesty: If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to. Truly excellent customer service: Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster. Escalate recurring integration failures to Product and Engineering as clear patterns, backed by evidence. Qualifications 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role, such as implementation, integration, solutions, or technical account management, ideally at an API platform. Clear written communication skills, including plans, handovers, and customer updates. Comfort working independently in a small regional team alongside a globally distributed function. Nice-to-Haves Knowledge of open banking, including UK Open Banking, PSD2/PSD3, AIS/PIS, and VRP. Domain depth in payments, identity verification, or credit and underwriting. Cross-functional Collaboration • Work closely with the Fraud & Risk Manager to ensure partner query intelligence and merchant monitoring findings are connected — a query from an acquirer about a specific merchant should inform, and be informed by, what you’re seeing in monitoring. • Liaise with the underwriting team where partner queries or merchant monitoring activity raises questions about how a merchant was onboarded or what their risk profile should be. • Support the engineering and product teams with information requests related to transaction tracing, where system-level investigation requires cross-functional input. • Contribute to the continuous improvement of response templates, internal runbooks, and query management procedures. What We’re Looking For Essential • Experience in a payments operations, risk operations, or financial crime role within a PSP, acquirer, payment facilitator, or bank — with direct exposure to acquirer or banking partner queries. • Demonstrable ability to trace transactions through payment systems — you understand how a payment moves, where it can go wrong, and how to reconstruct what happened from system data. • Strong written communication skills, with experience producing clear, structured responses to banking or regulatory counterparties who expect precision. • An investigative mindset — you ask the next question, not just the obvious one. Nice to Have • Familiarity with merchant risk monitoring in a PayFac or marketplace payments model. • Experience with chargeback and dispute management, including TC40/SAFE data or scheme fraud reporting. • Exposure to fraud tooling such as Fraud.net , Sift, SEON or equivalent platforms. • SQL or data querying skills for self-serve transaction investigation. High attention to detail and a commitment to patient safety and clinical governance. A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team. What do we offer? title: Medical Lead
description: Are you an experienced doctor with a passion for developing others and delivering exceptional patient care? At Montu, we are looking for a Medical Team Lead to join our growing Clinical team, combining clinical practice with the opportunity to lead, mentor and develop a team of doctors. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys supporting others, has experience providing clinical guidance and supervision, and is confident in building strong working relationships with clinicians and consultants. You will play a key role in supporting the professional development of our Junior Clinical Fellows (JCFs), helping them build confidence, develop greater clinical autonomy and deliver safe, high-quality patient care. As we continue to grow, this is an opportunity to bring your clinical expertise and leadership skills into an evolving area of healthcare, helping to shape and support the next generation of clinicians while making a meaningful difference to patients' lives. What is the job? As a Medical Team Lead, you will provide day-to-day leadership, support and guidance to a team of clinicians, ensuring they are well-supervised, well-supported, and progressing safely towards greater clinical autonomy. You will act as the primary link between clinicians and consultants, coordinating supervision, escalation pathways, and feedback loops so that patient care stays safe and consistent. You will combine your own clinical practice with people leadership, taking ownership of fellow development, consultant engagement, governance, and training within your team, while working alongside other Team Leads to keep standards consistent across the wider service. You will be the first point of contact for JCF’s requiring guidance on professional or personal development and appraisal or revalidation. You will also act as a trusted contact for consultants raising concerns about supervision and workload. What will you be doing? Clinician Line Management Act as the named line manager/lead for a cohort of clinicians, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, and pastoral support. Conduct regular 1:1s with each fellow, tracking progress against objectives, competencies, and rotation/training milestones. Identify clinicians who are struggling early, and put support plans in place in collaboration with consultants and HR/medical education leads. Assist with the onboarding and induction experience for new clinicians — inductions, shadowing, buddy systems, and early check-ins. Support the management of day-to-day workforce logistics for the clinicians: rota input, leave requests, sickness/absence, and shift coverage, working with the operations team. Recognise and celebrate good performance, and manage underperformance or conduct concerns through appropriate, documented processes alongside our HR team. Consultant Engagement Build and maintain strong working relationships with consultants. Act as the escalation point for consultants — surfacing concerns about supervision quality, caseload, or clinical support gaps. Coordinate consultant and JCF annual appraisals or revalidation. Gather and act on consultant feedback regarding clinical safety and any recurring themes. Support scheduling and coverage conversations with consultants (clinics, on-call, teaching sessions). Clinical & Patient Support Act as a point of escalation for complex clinical cases and patient concerns. Support clinicians through complaints, incidents, and governance issues involving their clinical decisions. Provide direct clinical mentoring, and know when to route a case to a consultant. Promote safe prescribing and adherence to clinical standards appropriate to clinicians’ training level. Governance, Quality & Audit Support compliance with clinical policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements across the fellow cohort. Support clinical audits and quality improvement projects, involving clinicians in QI work as a development opportunity. Analyse audit and incident themes specific to JCFs (e.g. common escalation triggers, training gaps) and use these to shape training priorities. Work with governance and operational teams on regulatory readiness. Operational Excellence & Change Monitor clinician workload, rota adherence, professionalism and service coverage; flag risks early. Contribute to process improvements that affect how fellows are supervised, escalate, or are trained. Track and report on team performance metrics: fellow progression, incident trends, audit outcomes, consultant feedback themes. Collaborate with other Team Leads to keep clinician management and consultant engagement approaches consistent across services. Training & Education Support the induction programmes for incoming clinicians from a medical perspective. Identify individual and cohort-wide development needs, working with consultants and training and education teams to close gaps. Involvement in the organisation and/or deliver teaching sessions and case reviews. Champion a culture of learning, feedback, and continuous improvement across the fellow-consultant relationship. This list is not exhaustive. As the business evolves, responsibilities may change and develop over time. What do you need? GMC registration with an active licence to practise and good professional standing. Experience supervising, managing, or mentoring junior doctors/clinical fellows is desirable. Experience working alongside or liaising with consultants in a clinical or operational capacity is desirable. Understanding of clinical governance, incident management, complaints handling, audit, and quality improvement. Confidence managing sensitive people-management conversations (performance, wellbeing, escalations). Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence both junior and senior clinicians. Experience working within digital healthcare, telemedicine, private healthcare, or fast-paced healthcare environments is desirable. Comfortable using clinical systems, rostering tools, and healthcare technology platforms. Adaptable, proactive, and solutions-focused, with a genuine interest in developing junior talent. title: Staff Software Engineer -  Promotions Platform
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 class="job-details__description-header text-color-secondary font-family-secondary" data-bind="i18n: 'job-details.employer-description-title'">About Us</h2> <div class="job-details__description-content basic-formatter" data-bind="html: pageData().job.corporateDescription"> <div>Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. </div> </div> <p> </p></div><h2 data-bind="i18n: 'job-details.organization-description-title'">About the Team</h2> <p><strong>Overview </strong></p> <p>Every time a fan places a bet, earns a reward, or checks out on Fanatics — Fanatics Core made that possible. We build the shared foundations — identity, payments, loyalty, wallet, data, and platform — that power sports betting, ecommerce, collectibles, and beyond. We supercharge the business by providing products and capabilities so that teams can focus on what matters most: building delightful experiences for the fans.</p> <p> </p> <p>As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll join the Promotions Platform team within FBG. Your duties will encompass the design, implementation, testing, and maintenance of software that enables customers to engage with FBG's promotional systems. Additionally, you will contribute to backend features that allow customers to earn rewards, which can be used throughout the entire Fanatics ecosystem. We are currently focused on developing the next generation of promotional tools.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a team or teams that develops, tests, documents, and deploys high quality software into production, leading the delivery of solutions that are extensible and scalable</li> <li>Clarify requirements and assists with coding/story estimates</li> <li>Participate in the on-call rotation when needed to troubleshoot software issues</li> <li>Quickly identify when to troubleshoot or escalate when tasks or projects hit roadblocks, find a path forward in difficult situations</li> <li>Mitigate immediate risk, identify and resolve root causes </li> <li>Remove bottlenecks and make technical and design approach trade-off decisions short term vs long-term</li> <li>Contribute to team planning and design discussions, building more expertise around design approaches, driving best practices and improving the speed of delivery</li> <li>Lead code reviews to provide constructive direction</li> <li>Proactively simplifies code and resolves team architecture deficiencies</li> <li>Impact software architecture, dependencies, performance, and business value</li> <li>Improve testability, operational excellence metrics, and team documentation</li> <li>Advise technology leaders, our product team, and other internal stakeholders to make technology decisions that grow and improve our products</li> <li>Mentor and coach other engineers and actively work to reduce onboarding burden of future team members</li> <li>Influence your team's adherence to the principles, guidelines, and best practices of our engineering strategy</li> <li>Develop a solid understanding of our industry, product, feature set and roadmap</li> <li>Remain current on the latest technologies and trends in software development</li> <li>Must be open to occasional travel to Fanatics Betting & Gaming offices and other locations for conferences, events, meetings, and team-building activities</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Required Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience building highly scalable and fault tolerant systems</li> <li>You understand a broad range of design approaches</li> <li>You are able to triage and debug system-wide production issues</li> <li>Demonstrated experience mentoring other engineers</li> <li>Able to effectively communicate complex technical subjects to a variety of audiences (engineers, technical leaders, marketing and operations teams, non-technical functional leaders)</li> <li>Familiar with Agile software product delivery and SCRUM methodology</li> <li>Excellent analytical and problem solving skills</li> <li>You have an agile mindset; able to embrace new initiatives in a fast-paced environment</li> <li>Thrives in an entrepreneurial, hyper-growth environment where priorities evolve regularly and decisions are made quickly</li> <li>Team-first mentality, with a willingness to do what it takes to get the job done and a desire to strive for better</li> <li>Able to effectively work cross-functionally within an enterprise environment</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience working in a start-up environment</li> <li>1+ years of experience leading a development team</li> <li>Experience with Java/Spring Boot</li> <li>Experience with React</li> <li>Experience with Apache Kafka</li> <li>Experience with AWS</li> <li>Experience with PostgreSQL</li> </ul> <p><em>If you possess some of these qualifications but not all of them, we still encourage you to apply!</em></p> <p>Depending on the role, your interview and onboarding experience may include in-person components, such as onsite interviews or Launching into Better: LIVE—a multi-day cultural immersion in New York City for full-time, non-seasonal hires. These sessions are designed to build connection and bring our culture to life, though specific travel and participation requirements will be confirmed based on your role and location. Your recruiter will provide clear guidance at each stage of the process.</p> <p>For information about our benefits, please visit <a href="https://benefitsatfanatics.com/">https://benefitsatfanatics.com/</a></p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p>Ranges will change based on country and state of residence, which are reflected in Geographical Zones defined by Fanatics Betting and Gaming. In addition to the base and bonus, full-time employment, and more. For information about our benefits, please visit <a href="https://benefitsatfanatics.com/">https://benefitsatfanatics.com/</a></p> <p> </p> <p> </p></div><div class="title">Salary Range</div><div class="pay-range"><span>€101.200</span><span class="divider">—</span><span>€126.500 EUR</span></div></div></div><div class="content-conclusion"><p></p> <p>By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ff494b9931735466ce28d5b/t/69de53bde2c02c25e9c38758/1776178110037/Candidate+Privacy+Policy+April+2026.pdf" target="_blank">Candidate Privacy Policy.</a></p> <p><em>Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process.
